intro = body("Water is always on the move. The sun's energy drives a continuous loop that carries water from the surface of the Earth up into the atmosphere and back down again. This loop is called the water cycle. In this lesson you will learn its three main stages, work through an example, and check your understanding.")

h1 = heading("1. Evaporation")
p1 = paragraph("The sun heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers. Some of the liquid turns into water vapor, an invisible gas that rises into the air. Plants also release water vapor through their leaves, which is called transpiration.")

h2 = heading("2. Condensation")
p2 = paragraph("As water vapor rises, it cools. Cool air cannot hold as much vapor, so the vapor turns back into tiny liquid droplets. These droplets gather around dust particles and group together to form clouds.")
c2 = callout("info", "Key idea", "Condensation is the opposite of evaporation: a gas cools and becomes a liquid.")

h3 = heading("3. Precipitation and Collection")
p3 = paragraph("When cloud droplets grow heavy enough, they fall as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. This is precipitation. The water then flows over land into streams and rivers, soaks into the ground, or fills lakes and oceans. This is collection, and the cycle begins again.")
c3 = callout("tip", "Key idea", "Precipitation returns water to the surface, where it is collected and can evaporate once more.")
